title: Airport
subtitle: Bring Arrow Flight services into your SQL.
intro: Attach an Arrow Flight service as a DuckDB catalog, then query its tables alongside local data. Discover available flights, fetch a descriptor directly, and invoke server-defined actions when a full catalog is unnecessary.

reference.name: ATTACH … (TYPE airport)
reference.description: Mount a compatible Flight catalog under a DuckDB alias.

reference.name: airport_databases(url)
reference.description: Discover databases exposed by the server.

reference.name: airport_flights(url)
reference.description: List available flight descriptors and metadata.

reference.name: airport_take_flight(url, descriptor)
reference.description: Read a specific flight directly as a table.

reference.name: airport_action(url, action, body)
reference.description: Invoke a server-defined action; available actions vary.

reference.name: CREATE SECRET … (TYPE airport)
reference.description: Scope a bearer token to a Flight URL prefix.

reference.name: airport_version()
reference.description: Identify the loaded Airport build for diagnostics.

notes.title: Capabilities come from the server
notes.body: Catalog discovery, filter pushdown and writes depend on the Flight server's Airport-compatible interfaces. A service using Arrow internally does not necessarily expose those interfaces. Check its schema and capabilities before attaching.

notes.title: Authenticate by URL scope
notes.body: Use an airport secret with scope and auth_token for protected services. Use grpc+tls for TLS endpoints. Server-defined descriptors, table names and actions must match the service you connect to.
